In Fukuoka, the udon is soft on purpose, the mackerel is eaten raw, and the hotpot ends with a pile of noodles. Most visitors only eat the ramen. Here's how locals eat the rest 👇

🍜 Hungry yet? The spots, hours and prices 👉 https://japanbystation.com/fukuoka-food-beyond-tonkotsu-ramen

🍥 HAKATA UDON

Soft and tender, in a clear broth of flying fish, anchovy, bonito and kelp, with goboten (burdock tempura) on top. At Makino Udon, by Hakata Station, each bowl comes with a little kettle of extra broth, because the noodles keep drinking it up.

🐟 GOMA SABA

Raw mackerel in sesame-soy. Mackerel spoils fast, so most of Japan doesn't eat it raw. Fukuoka's fresh catch makes it possible. Hakata Gomasaba-ya near Akasaka serves it at lunch for ¥1,000.

🍲 MOTSUNABE

A beef offal hotpot. The local move is the finish: champon noodles go into the broth at the end. Pace yourself.

🐔 MIZUTAKI

A chicken hotpot where you drink a cup of the plain broth before anything goes in.

🍜 AND THE RAMEN, ORDERED PROPERLY

Say your firmness (barikata = a little firm), and when the noodles are gone, order kaedama, a refill for your soup. Fukuoka's tourism site suggests one step softer the second time, because the soup has cooled.

We checked every hour and price against the shops' listings before putting this up.
